name: PapillArray tactile sensor (Dev Kit v2)

sources.title: Q. Wang, P. M. Ulloa, R. Burke, D. Cordova Bulens and S. J. Redmond, "Robust Learning-Based Incipient Slip Detection using the PapillArray Optical Tactile Sensor for Improved Robotic Gripping", arXiv:2307.04011
sources.covers: sensor description: a square array of nine elastic silicone pillars with different heights, x-y-z force per pillar at 1,000 Hz; Dev Kit v1 and v2 differ in size and pillar hardness

note: A contact sensor, modelled by pad coverage, not a workspace camera, so it has no imagers. A commercial pillar-array tactile sensor (Contactile, Australia). The maker's pages could not be fetched on 2026-11-07 (the site did not answer), so the figures are from a paper that used it: "a square array of nine elastic silicone pillars with varying unloaded heights" (taxels 9), each giving "x-y-z force data ... at a high sampling rate of 1,000 Hz" (entered as fps). The sensing principle is optical (the paper's title: "PapillArray Optical Tactile Sensor"). The pad size is not stated in that paper, so pad_mm is null; a later paper gives about 24 x 24 mm, not entered. Not stated: power, mass, size, interface (the kit has a controller and a USB cable). Its readings are not an image stream, so no stream is entered; the bandwidth budget needs the data rate as a measured or stated figure.
